question_text: Juan is a 67-year-old natural-born Filipino citizen who has resided in the Philippines for the past 15 years. He was convicted of a crime involving moral turpitude (estafa) and sentenced to 2 years imprisonment, which he served fully. He has since completed his sentence and has not been convicted of any other crime. Which of the following statements about Juan's right to vote in the next national election is correct?

options.text: Juan may vote because he is a citizen and resident, and his conviction does not permanently disqualify him.
Juan may not vote because he is over 65 years old, which is the maximum voting age under the Constitution.
Juan may not vote because his conviction for a crime involving moral turpitude carries a permanent disqualification.
Juan may vote only if he applies for and is granted an absolute pardon from the President.
